Given a finite group G G with a normal subgroup N N , the simple graph Γ G ​ ( N ) \Gamma_{\textit{G}}(\textit{N}) is a graph whose vertices are of the form | x G | |x^{G}| , where x ∈ N ∖ Z ⁡ ( G ) x\in{N\setminus{Z(G)}} , and x G x^{G} is the G G -conjugacy class of N N containing the element x x .

arxiv-2208-08150.title: Capturing usage patterns in bike sharing system via multilayer network fused Lasso
arxiv-2208-08150.creator: Yunjin Choi, Haeran Cho, Hyelim Son
arxiv-2208-08150.description: Abstract Data collected from a bike-sharing system exhibit complex temporal and spatial features. We analyze shared-bike usage data collected in three large cities at the level of individual stations, accounting for station-specific behavior and covariate effects. For this, we adopt a penalized regression approach with a multilayer network fused Lasso penalty.

arxiv-2302-03413.title: Inflation vs. Ekpyrosis — comparing stability in general non-minimal theory
arxiv-2302-03413.creator: Debottam Nandi, Manjeet Kaur
arxiv-2302-03413.description: Abstract The scalar field is considered to have dominated the early Universe. One subtle yet crucial requirement of this assumption is that the solution must be highly stable, i.e., indifferent to any initial conditions because there are no favored ones.

arxiv-2307-07852.title: Determination of Lens Mass Density Profile from Strongly-Lensed Gravitational-Wave Signals
arxiv-2307-07852.creator: Mick Wright, Justin Janquart, Martin Hendry
arxiv-2307-07852.description: Abstract As the interferometers detecting gravitational waves are upgraded, improving their sensitivity, the probability of observing strong lensing increases. Once a detection is made, it will be critical to gain as much information as possible about the lensing object from these observations.

arxiv-2308-02364.title: Matrix Completion When Missing Is Not at Random and Its Applications in Causal Panel Data Models This research was supported by NSF Grants DMS-2015285 and DMS-2052955, and NIH Grant R01-HG01073.
arxiv-2308-02364.creator: Jungjun Choi and Ming Yuan Department of Statistics Columbia University
arxiv-2308-02364.description: Abstract This paper develops an inferential framework for matrix completion when missing is not at random and without the requirement of strong signals. Our development is based on the observation that if the number of missing entries is small enough compared to the panel size, then they can be estimated well even when missing is not at random.

arxiv-2409-09877.title: REG: Refined Generalized Focal Loss for Road Asset Detection on Thai Highways Using Vision-Based Detection and Segmentation Models
arxiv-2409-09877.creator: Teerapong Panboonyuen
arxiv-2409-09877.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Teerapong Panboonyuen. This paper introduces a novel framework for detecting and segmenting critical road assets on Thai highways using an advanced Re fined G eneralized Focal Loss (REG) formulation. Integrated into state-of-the-art vision-based detection and segmentation models, the proposed method effectively addresses class imbalance and the challenges of localizing small, underrepresented road elements, including pavilions, pedestrian bridges, information signs, single-arm poles, bus stops, warning signs, and concrete guardrails.

arxiv-2409-12334.title: Deep vessel segmentation with joint multi-prior encoding
arxiv-2409-12334.creator: A. Sadikine, B. Badic, E. Ferrante, V. Noblet, P. Ballet, D. Visvikis, P.-H. Conze
arxiv-2409-12334.description: Abstract The precise delineation of blood vessels in medical images is critical for many clinical applications, including pathology detection and surgical planning. However, fully-automated vascular segmentation is challenging because of the variability in shape, size, and topology. Manual segmentation remains the gold standard but is time-consuming, subjective, and impractical for large-scale studies.

arxiv-2409-17089.title: Quantum Advantage in Distributed Sensing with Noisy Quantum Networks
arxiv-2409-17089.creator: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, Zain H. Saleem
arxiv-2409-17089.description: Abstract We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks which only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-diagonal probe states, a representative distributed sensing scenario.

arxiv-2411-09579.title: Propensity Score Matching: Should We Use It in Designing Observational Studies?
arxiv-2411-09579.creator: Fei Wan
arxiv-2411-09579.description: Abstract Background: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) stands as a widely embraced method in comparative effectiveness research. PSM crafts matched datasets, mimicking some attributes of randomized designs, from observational data. In a valid PSM design where all baseline confounders are measured and matched, the confounders would be balanced, allowing the treatment status to be considered as if it were randomly assigned.

arxiv-2501-14135.title: The Wasserstein space of stochastic processes in continuous time
arxiv-2501-14135.creator: D. Bartl, M. Beiglböck, G. Pammer, S. Schrott, X. Zhang
arxiv-2501-14135.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by D. Bartl, M. Beiglböck, G. Pammer, S. Schrott, X. Zhang. Researchers from different areas have independently defined extensions of the usual weak convergence of laws of stochastic processes with the goal of adequately accounting for the flow of information. Natural approaches are convergence of the Aldous–Knight prediction process, Hellwig’s information topology, convergence in adapted distribution in the sense of Hoover–Keisler and the weak topology induced by optimal stopping problems.

arxiv-2502-06175.title: Reducing Alert Fatigue via AI-Assisted Negotiation: A Case for Dependabot
arxiv-2502-06175.creator: Raula Gaikovina Kula
arxiv-2502-06175.description: Abstract The increasing complexity of software dependencies has led to the emergence of automated dependency management tools, such as Dependabot. However, these tools often overwhelm developers with a high volume of alerts and notifications, leading to alert fatigue. This paper presents a position on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents as dependency negotiators to reduce alert fatigue.

pmc-10525965.title: The Direction of the Antibacterial Effect of Rutin Hydrate and Amikacin
pmc-10525965.creator: Maria Miklasińska-Majdanik, Małgorzata Kępa, Tomasz J Wąsik, Karolina Zapletal-Pudełko, Magdalena Klim, Robert D Wojtyczka, Marc Maresca, Mihaela Niculae, Daniela Hanganu
pmc-10525965.description: The aim of the presented study was to examine the in vitro antimicrobial activity of rutin hydrate (RH) alone and in combination with amikacin against 12 reference strains of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The antibacterial activity assay was evaluated in the concentration range of 2–2048 µg/mL.

pmc-10695646.title: Association of Plant-Based Protein Intake with Cognitive Function in Adults with CKD
pmc-10695646.creator: Luis Perez, Zhiying You, Jessica Kendrick
pmc-10695646.description: r dementia. This cognitive decline contributes to excessive rates of physical/functional decline, reduced quality of life, and mortality in the CKD population. It is of utmost importance to identify ways to reduce cognitive impairment in CKD. In the general aging population, a Mediterranean diet has been associated with cognitive performance.

pmc-11594102.title: TPGPred: A Mixed-Feature-Driven Approach for Identifying Thermophilic Proteins Based on GradientBoosting
pmc-11594102.creator: Cuihuan Zhao, Shuan Yan, Jiahang Li, Jorge Mateo
pmc-11594102.description: Thermophilic proteins maintain their stability and functionality under extreme high-temperature conditions, making them of significant importance in both fundamental biological research and biotechnological applications. In this study, we developed a machine learning-based thermophilic protein GradientBoosting prediction model, TPGPred, designed to predict thermophilic proteins by leveraging a large-scale dataset of both thermophilic and non-thermophilic protein sequences.

pmc-11599336.title: Non-operative treatment of metacarpal fractures and patient-reported outcomes: a multicentre snapshot study
pmc-11599336.creator: L. E. M. de Haas, P. A. Jawahier, T. C. C. Hendriks, D. A. Salentijn, B. T. van Hoorn, R. H. H. Groenwold, N. W. L. Schep, M. van Heijl
pmc-11599336.description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate practice variation in non-operative treatment methods and immobilisation duration for metacarpal fractures, and to evaluate patient-reported outcomes.MethodsConducted in 12 Dutch hospitals over three months in 2020, this study included adult patients with non-operatively treated solitary metacarpal fractures. Fractures were classified into intra-articular base, extra-articular base, shaft, neck, and intra-articular head fractures.

pmc-13135071.title: Association Between Childhood Behavioral Problems and Parental Military Active Duty Status: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2017-2021 National Survey of Children’s Health
pmc-13135071.creator: Kayla L Haydon, Vanessa C Kady, Chrisnel Lamy, Marcia Varella
pmc-13135071.description: IntroductionChildren of military families face unique stressors, including frequent relocations and parental deployments, which can disrupt stability and influence behavioral development. These experiences may also contribute to conduct problems and challenges in social interactions, including bullying victimization and perpetration. However, limited research exists specifically examining behavioral risks in military-connected children.

pmc-13266751.title: Acute Myocardial Injury in the Setting of Hypertensive Emergency: A Case Report
pmc-13266751.creator: Selma Saidi, Mehdi Moujahid, Zineb Mehssani, Zayna Nadhil, Nadia Fellat
pmc-13266751.description: Hypertensive emergency can cause acute myocardial injury characterized by chest pain, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and ischemic electrocardiographic changes in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. This presentation reflects a mismatch between myocardial oxygen supply and demand, driven by severe afterload increase, microvascular dysfunction, and subendocardial ischemia.

pmc-13285415.title: Exploring how men and women improve their relationships through participation in HIKA, a group-based, couples-focused IPV prevention program in the Democratic Republic of Congo
pmc-13285415.creator: Anjalee Kohli, Nancy Perrin, Clovis M Mitima, Roméo R Binwa, Davy R Mpanano, Jean B Heri, Jeannette N Cinogerwa, Gisèle N Mushengezi, Arsene B Kajabika, Marie C Nakesa, Joëlle B Balibuno, Alfred M Bacikenge, Émilie Awa, Julien A Lubala, Remy M Mpanano, Nancy Glass
pmc-13285415.description: Group-based IPV prevention programmes use participatory learning to impart new information, encourage critical reflection on gender and power dynamics, and develop new skills. Understanding whether and how these programmes are internalised and acted upon can allow for programme designs to enhance facilitators of positive change, inform efforts to adapt and scale the programme, and understand the potential for sustained change.

pmc-13406661.title: Narrative Review of the Pathophysiology of Post-Infectious Bronchiolitis Obliterans
pmc-13406661.creator: Alessandro Zago, Caterina Cocchi, Massimo Maschio, Laura Badina, Francesca Policastro, Alessandro Amaddeo, Egidio Barbi, Sergio Ghirardo
pmc-13406661.description: Post-Infectious Bronchiolitis Obliterans (PIBO) is a rare chronic obstructive lung disease characterized by irreversible airflow limitation due to inflammation, fibrosis, and obliteration of the small airways following severe lower respiratory tract infection. Adenovirus is the most frequently associated pathogen, followed by other viruses and atypical bacteria.

pmc-13439476.title: Transforming preservice teachers’ emotions and appraisals on outdoor learning in early childhood education
pmc-13439476.creator: Cristina Valares-Masa, José María Marcos-Merino, Jesús A. Gómez-Ochoa de Alda
pmc-13439476.description: Outdoor learning offers well-documented benefits for children’s health and learning, yet its integration into Early Childhood Education remains limited, partly due to barriers related to teacher preparation. This study investigates the impact of an educational intervention designed to integrate outdoor learning across the early childhood curriculum on preservice teachers’ appraisals, emotions, and perceived preparedness.

pmc-13469565.title: Real-world outcomes and safety of inetetamab plus pyrotinib and chemotherapy in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer: A multicenter retrospective study
pmc-13469565.creator: Fan Wu, Cailing Lin, Zhiwu Lin, Qingmo Yang, Xiuping Wu, Biyin Chen, Nani Li, Ruxue Zhang, Xiufeng Wu, Weiwei Huang, Xinhua Chen, Yi Hong, Kan Chen, Jian Liu
pmc-13469565.description: BackgroundInetetamab and pyrotinib have shown promising activity in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC). However, real-world data on their combination with chemotherapy (IPyC) across different treatment lines remain limited.ObjectivesThis multicenter retrospective study aimed to describe the outcomes associated with a dual HER2-targeting strategy IPyC in HER2-positive MBC across treatment lines in real-world clinical practice.DesignMulticenter retrospective study.

(a) Purchase Authorized.— The Secretary may, instead of or in addition to underwriting the insurance program through the Fund, purchase from one or more insurance companies a policy or policies of group insurance in order to provide the benefits.
